name: Composition / layout system
controls: How elements are arranged within the frame, which layout system organizes them, what leads the eye, and how that arrangement changes over time.
question: How should things be arranged on screen, and how should the layout evolve?
notes: Composition options stack: a piece can be UI-led, use a bento grid and follow a temporal composition all at once, which is why up to three can be picked. Families mix three kinds of choice: framing (where the eye goes), layout systems (the grid), and containers or contexts (cards, devices, canvases). The 'led' options name the dominant element. TEMPORAL COMPOSITION: motion design is never one layout. A frame may begin as a single centered element, transform into a multi-card grid, then expand into full-screen UI; the composition is the sequence of layouts, not any one frame. Each layout in the sequence is a keyframe of the composition, and the transition between two layouts is itself a design decision: which element persists and becomes the anchor (the hero card grows into the screen), which elements are born from it (cards split out of the centered object), which leave, and what path, easing and timing they use. Good temporal composition keeps at least one element continuous across every layout change so the eye never loses its place (GSAP Flip is the tool: record, relayout, animate from the old state). It also manages density over time: sparse, then dense, then sparse again gives rhythm; staying dense tires the viewer. When the director picks temporal composition, the other picked options become the states it moves through. 'Bento grid' and 'infinite canvas' are recent informal industry terms; 'Swiss grid' refers to the International Typographic Style.

options.what: One primary element placed at the optical center with everything else subordinate or absent.
options.looks: A single headline, product or UI element in the middle, generous margins, symmetric breathing room.
options.motion: Push-ins toward center, elements emerging from and returning to the middle, radial reveals.
options.use: Title cards, logo reveals, feature statements, keynote-style product reveals.
options.vs: Symmetrical composition balances multiple elements across an axis; centered hero is about one element. Single-object hero specifies a physical object.
options.prompt: Place the single key element at the optical center (2-3% above geometric center), occupying 30-50% of frame width, with nothing else on screen except at most one small label. Enter and exit from the center; background stays plain.

options.what: Elements weighted to one side and balanced by negative space or a smaller counterweight.
options.looks: Headline left, visual right (or top-left anchor), rule-of-thirds placement, deliberate imbalance.
options.motion: Lateral movement across the frame, elements sliding into their third, parallax between sides.
options.use: Editorial product films, feature explainers, brand manifestos.
options.vs: Editorial grid is a systematic structure that often produces asymmetry; asymmetric composition is the balance principle itself.
options.prompt: Weight the frame to one side: primary element on the left third (x 8-45%), a smaller counterweight on the right third, 30%+ empty. Move elements laterally along the thirds; never center the main element.

options.what: Elements mirrored across a vertical or horizontal axis.
options.looks: Mirror-balanced pairs, center axis, formal stability; Wes Anderson-style framing.
options.motion: Mirrored motion from both sides, center-out expansions, symmetric wipes.
options.use: Comparisons, luxury and formal brands, before/after reveals, title sequences.
options.vs: Centered hero is one element; symmetrical composition mirrors several. Split screen divides into panels that need not mirror.
options.prompt: Mirror every element across the vertical center axis: matched pairs at equal distances, identical sizes, animated simultaneously with mirrored directions (left element moves from -x, right from +x, same ease and duration).

options.what: A strict column-and-baseline grid from the International Typographic Style, with flush-left type and objective hierarchy.
options.looks: Visible or implied columns, flush-left ragged-right text, large neo-grotesk headlines, photographs cropped to grid fields, lots of white space.
options.motion: Elements move and snap by whole columns, rule lines draw across the grid, blocks reflow.
options.use: Cultural and corporate identities, design-led tech brands, event graphics.
options.vs: Modular grid adds rows to form cells; editorial grid mixes column spans more freely; bento is a card mosaic. Swiss grid is a typographic system first.
refs: Josef Müller-Brockmann, Grid Systems in Graphic Design (1981)
options.prompt: Lay out on a 12-column grid (80px margins, 24px gutters on 1920x1080) with an 8px baseline; all type flush-left in a neo-grotesk, headlines spanning 6-9 columns; thin 2px rules on column edges. Move elements only in whole-column increments.

options.what: A grid of columns and rows forming equal cells (modules) that content occupies in multiples.
options.looks: Regular repeating cells, even gutters, content snapping to 1x1, 2x1, 2x2 modules; strong rhythm.
options.motion: Cells filling in sequence (row-wise, diagonal or random stagger), modules swapping, grid rearranging.
options.use: Feature overviews, product catalogs, data dashboards, systematic brand layouts.
options.vs: Bento grid uses unequal, deliberately varied cards as a mosaic; a modular grid uses equal modules. Swiss grid is primarily columns.
options.prompt: Divide the frame into a 6x4 modular grid of equal cells (24px gutters, 80px margins); every element occupies whole modules. Reveal cells with a diagonal stagger (stagger { each: 0.04, grid: [4,6], from: 'start' }).

options.what: A mosaic of rounded cards of varied sizes packed into a rectangle, each card holding one feature or idea.
options.looks: Rounded cards (radius 24-32px), unequal spans (one large hero card plus smaller ones), consistent gutters, each card a mini-composition.
options.motion: Cards assemble in staggered sequence, the hero card expands to full screen, cards swap content in place.
options.use: Feature summaries in launch films, landing pages, keynote recap slides.
options.conveys: Richness, modern product polish, 'everything in one view'.
options.vs: A modular grid uses equal cells; bento deliberately varies card sizes. The term is informal, popularized by Apple keynote feature summaries around 2022-23.
options.prompt: Pack 5-7 rounded cards (radius 28px, 20px gutters) into a 1600x900 rectangle: one hero card spanning 2x2, the rest 1x1 and 2x1. Each card holds one feature (icon, number or UI crop plus a 2-4 word label). Assemble with stagger 70ms, scale 0.92 to 1, 500ms ease power3.out.

options.what: A magazine-style layout mixing column spans, pull quotes, captions and imagery with deliberate hierarchy.
options.looks: Large serif or grotesk headlines, image blocks spanning uneven columns, small captions, folios and rules.
options.motion: Page-like transitions, images sliding into their frames, captions arriving after images.
options.use: Brand stories, editorial explainers, luxury and culture brands, annual reports.
options.vs: Swiss grid is strict and objective; editorial grid breaks the grid for emphasis. Poster composition is one big statement; editorial is multi-element.
options.prompt: Use a 12-column editorial grid: headline spans columns 1-8, a portrait image block columns 9-12 extending past the top margin, captions at 18-20px under images, 1px rules and a small folio label. Reveal image blocks with clip-path wipes before their captions.

options.what: The frame divided into two or more panels showing different content simultaneously.
options.looks: Vertical or horizontal divisions, contrasting content per panel, sometimes a moving divider.
options.motion: Divider slides to reveal, panels push each other, synchronized actions across panels.
options.use: Before/after, comparisons, multi-platform demos, cause and effect.
options.vs: Symmetrical composition mirrors; split screen juxtaposes different content.
options.prompt: Divide the frame vertically 50/50 (or 60/40) with a 2px divider; left panel shows the old state, right the new. Animate the divider sliding from 0% to 50% over 800ms ease power3.inOut to reveal the comparison; keep actions synchronized across panels.

options.what: Cards layered on top of each other like a deck, with the top card in focus.
options.looks: Offset stack (each card 12-20px lower and 4-6% smaller), top card sharp, lower cards dimmed.
options.motion: Cards swipe away to reveal the next, the stack reorders, cards fan out.
options.use: Notifications, sequential feature reveals, mobile app demos, testimonials.
options.vs: Floating cards are spread in space; stacked cards overlap on one axis. A carousel moves cards laterally.
options.prompt: Stack 3-4 cards: each lower card offset y +16px, scale -5%, and brightness -10%. Advance by swiping the top card out (x 120%, rotation 8 degrees, 450ms ease power3.in) while the rest move up one position (400ms ease power3.out).

options.what: UI cards or panels scattered in space at different depths, gently drifting.
options.looks: Several cards at varied scales and z-depths, soft shadows, slight rotations, parallax.
options.motion: Slow drifting (sine), parallax on camera moves, cards converging into a layout.
options.use: Landing-page heroes, feature overviews, SaaS launch intros.
options.vs: Stacked cards overlap in a deck; floating cards spread through space. Layered depth is the underlying principle.
options.prompt: Scatter 4-6 UI cards at three depth levels (scale 1.0, 0.8, 0.6 with blur 0, 1, 3px), rotations within +-4 degrees, soft shadows. Drift each y +-10px on independent 3-5s sine cycles; move deeper cards 40% less on camera pans.

options.what: A row of items that scrolls laterally with one item in focus.
options.looks: Centered focus item with neighbors partially visible at the edges, sometimes scaled down.
options.motion: Lateral slides with snap, focus item scaling up, 3D coverflow rotation.
options.use: Template showcases, product ranges, feature lists, portfolio reels.
options.vs: Stacked cards advance in depth; carousel advances laterally. Timeline implies chronology.
options.prompt: Arrange 5+ items in a horizontal row, focus item centered at scale 1, neighbors at 0.85 and 60% opacity, 40px gaps. Advance one item every 1.2-1.8s: row x shifts one slot in 600ms ease power3.inOut with focus scaling in sync.

options.what: Events laid out along a line representing time.
options.looks: A horizontal or vertical axis with markers, dates and event cards.
options.motion: Line draws forward, camera tracks along it, markers pop as the line reaches them.
options.use: Company history, roadmaps, changelogs, process stories.
options.vs: Flowchart shows logic and branching; timeline shows chronology. Carousel is browsing, not time.
options.prompt: Draw a 2px horizontal line across the frame with evenly spaced circular markers (12px) and event cards above/below alternately. Animate the line drawing left to right while the camera tracks; each marker scales in as the line reaches it, its card following 120ms later.

options.what: Steps as boxes connected by directional arrows showing process and decisions.
options.looks: Rounded boxes, arrow connectors, decision diamonds, orthogonal or curved lines.
options.motion: Connectors draw on in sequence, a pulse travels along the path, boxes light up as reached.
options.use: Workflow automation, integrations, how-it-works explainers, developer tools.
options.conveys: Logic, process, clarity of cause and effect.
options.vs: Node map is a non-linear network; flowchart has a direction and sequence.
options.prompt: Lay out 4-7 rounded boxes (radius 12px) left to right or top to bottom joined by 2px orthogonal connectors with arrowheads. Draw each connector (stroke-dashoffset, 350ms) then activate the next box (border to accent color, scale 1.04); send a small glowing dot along the finished path.

options.what: Entities as nodes connected by edges in a non-linear network.
options.looks: Circles or cards connected by lines, clusters, a central hub, varied node sizes.
options.motion: Nodes pop in and edges draw between them, data pulses along edges, force-layout settling.
options.use: Integrations, AI and knowledge graphs, infrastructure, social and network products.
options.vs: Flowchart is sequential; node map is relational. Radial and orbit compositions are special symmetric cases.
options.prompt: Place 8-20 nodes (circles 24-64px) around a larger hub, joined by 1.5px edges at 40% opacity. Reveal nodes from the hub outward (stagger 50ms, scale 0 to 1, ease back.out(1.7)), draw edges after both endpoints exist, then send 4px pulses along edges.

options.what: Elements arranged around a central point, radiating outward.
options.looks: A center element with items on a circle or in rings, spokes, concentric arrangement.
options.motion: Items fan out from center, rings expand, rotation around the center.
options.use: Ecosystem overviews, integrations, product-at-the-center stories.
options.conveys: Centrality, completeness, the product as hub.
options.vs: Orbit composition has elements continuously circling; radial is a static arrangement around a center.
options.prompt: Place the key element at center and 6-10 items evenly on a circle of radius 320px (on 1080p), optional spokes. Fan items out from center to the circle, 500ms ease power3.out, stagger 40ms clockwise.

options.what: Elements circling a center on elliptical paths, often at different speeds and radii.
options.looks: Concentric thin orbit rings, small icons or logos riding them, center object.
options.motion: Continuous rotation along orbits, perspective ellipses, items entering orbit.
options.use: Integration ecosystems, AI and platform products, space-themed brand films.
options.conveys: Gravity, ecosystem, the product as center of the universe.
options.vs: Radial is static; orbit moves continuously.
options.prompt: Draw 2-3 concentric 1px rings (radii 220, 360, 500px) around the center object; place 3-5 logos on each, rotating 360 degrees per 20-40s, inner rings faster, ease none. Tilt the system rotationX 60 degrees for perspective ellipses if depth is wanted.

options.what: Imagery, color or UI extends to every edge of the frame with no margins.
options.looks: Edge-to-edge content, no frames or containers, immersive.
options.motion: Push-ins, pans across the content, full-frame transitions and wipes.
options.use: Footage, big product shots, color-field title cards, full-screen UI moments.
options.vs: Poster composition may be full bleed but is organized around one graphic statement; full bleed only means no margins.
options.prompt: Run the key image, color field or UI to all four frame edges with no margins or containers; overlay type directly with safe margins of 80px. Transition between full-bleed shots with full-frame wipes or push transitions.

options.what: Empty space dominates the frame and shapes attention toward small elements.
options.looks: One small element, 70-90% empty frame, restrained color, precise placement.
options.motion: Minimal, slow, one element at a time; long holds.
options.use: Luxury brands, premium hardware, AI and research brands, contemplative moments.
options.vs: Sparse typography is a type density choice; negative-space composition governs the whole frame.
options.prompt: Keep 75-90% of the frame empty; place one small element (10-20% of frame width) off-center on a third. One element enters at a time, moving slowly (1-1.5s, ease power2.out), with holds of 2s+.

options.what: Each frame composed as a complete graphic poster: one bold statement with strong hierarchy.
options.looks: Huge type or image, strong color blocks, few elements, graphic punch, often full bleed.
options.motion: Hard cuts between poster frames, kinetic builds of each poster, graphic wipes.
options.use: Event promos, brand stings, social ads, music and culture content.
options.vs: Editorial grid has multiple elements in hierarchy; poster composition has one message per frame.
options.prompt: Compose every frame as a standalone poster: one statement at 200px+ or one image filling 60%+, one accent color block, one small info line. Build each poster in under 600ms and cut to the next on the beat.

options.what: Mixed cut-out images, textures, type and shapes layered with overlap and rotation.
options.looks: Torn or cut edges, overlapping photos and paper, rotated elements, mixed scales, tape and stickers.
options.motion: Stop-motion stepping, elements slapped on, parallax between layers.
options.use: Culture and lifestyle brands, social content, music, community stories.
options.vs: Floating cards are clean UI in space; collage mixes media with deliberate roughness.
options.prompt: Layer 8-15 cut-out elements (photos with 4px white borders, torn paper, type, stickers) with rotations of +-12 degrees and overlaps. Add each on a stepped rhythm (steps(1), one element every 3-4 frames at 12fps) and give layers slight parallax.

options.what: A large continuous 2D workspace the camera pans and zooms across.
options.looks: Boards, frames and objects spread across a big plane, dotted grid background, zoomed views.
options.motion: Camera pans and zooms between areas, zoom-out reveals of the whole canvas.
options.use: Whiteboard and design tools, brainstorming products, overview-to-detail stories.
options.vs: Desktop workspace shows OS windows; infinite canvas is one app's endless plane. The term comes from tools such as Figma, Miro and tldraw.
options.prompt: Build a 6000x4000px canvas with a 24px dot grid and content clusters; move a camera container with x/y/scale tweens (800-1200ms ease power3.inOut) between clusters, ending with a zoom-out to show the whole canvas.

options.what: A composed scene drawn in isometric projection (equal 120-degree axes, no vanishing point).
options.looks: Objects on a 30-degree grid, blocks and platforms, miniature-world feel, no perspective distortion.
options.motion: Objects rise from the ground plane, flows move along isometric paths, camera pans laterally.
options.use: Infrastructure, data flows, logistics, systems explainers.
options.conveys: System overview, orderliness, a 'city' of parts.
options.vs: Layered depth uses perspective and parallax; isometric has no vanishing point, so parallax does not apply.
options.prompt: Draw the scene on an isometric grid (axes at 30 degrees from horizontal, CSS transform rotateX(60deg) rotateZ(-45deg) or pre-drawn), objects as flat-shaded blocks with three face tones. Raise objects from y +40px to 0 staggered 60ms; animate flows along grid axes only.

options.what: The frame shows an operating-system desktop with multiple app windows.
options.looks: Windows with title bars, dock or taskbar, wallpaper, overlapping apps.
options.motion: Windows open, resize and rearrange, cursor moves between apps, drag and drop across windows.
options.use: Productivity tools, integrations between apps, OS-level utilities.
options.vs: Browser window frames one web app; desktop workspace shows multiple apps and the OS.
options.prompt: Show a simplified desktop: soft gradient wallpaper, 2-3 app windows with 12px corner radius and 36px title bars, a minimal dock. Open windows with scale 0.92 to 1 and opacity over 350ms ease power3.out; move content between windows with drag-and-drop cursor actions.

options.what: The product appears inside a browser frame.
options.looks: Simplified browser chrome (traffic lights, URL bar), web app content inside, often floating with a shadow.
options.motion: Scroll inside the window, the window scales up to full screen, URL typing.
options.use: Web app launches, website showcases, SaaS demos.
options.conveys: This is a real web product; accessibility, no install.
options.vs: Desktop workspace includes the OS; browser window isolates one web product.
options.prompt: Frame the product in a minimal browser window: 12px radius, 44px chrome bar with three 12px circles and a pill URL field, 1440x900 content area scaled to 80% of frame width, shadow 0 30px 80px rgba(0,0,0,0.25). Scroll content inside with smooth y tweens.

options.what: A phone or phone screen is the central object of the frame.
options.looks: A device (or bezel-less screen with rounded corners) centered or angled, UI inside, often with hand or floating elements around it.
options.motion: Phone rotates into view, screens swipe, UI elements pop out of the screen.
options.use: Mobile app launches, app store previews, social-first ads.
options.vs: Device ecosystem shows several devices; phone composition focuses on one.
options.prompt: Place one phone (screen corner radius 55px on a 390x844 screen scaled to 70% of frame height) centered or rotated 8-15 degrees; animate UI inside with swipes and taps, and let 1-2 UI elements pop out of the screen plane with shadow for emphasis.

options.what: Several devices (phone, tablet, laptop, watch) arranged together showing one product across platforms.
options.looks: A family of devices at related scales, consistent UI across them, grouped or staggered in depth.
options.motion: Devices arrive in sequence, content syncs across devices, camera sweeps past the group.
options.use: Cross-platform launches, sync features, platform brands.
options.conveys: Continuity, ubiquity, a platform rather than an app.
options.vs: Phone composition features one device; floating cards float UI fragments rather than devices.
options.prompt: Group laptop, tablet and phone at realistic relative scales, overlapping in depth (laptop back, phone front). Bring them in staggered 150ms from below, then show sync: an action on the phone triggers the same state change on the others 200ms later.

options.what: Flat elements separated into planes at different depths so they parallax.
options.looks: 2.5D stacking, planes at different scales, depth blur on far layers, overlapping.
options.motion: Parallax on camera moves, layers separating (exploded view), z-axis push-ins.
options.use: Hero sequences, UI breakdowns, illustration-led explainers.
options.conveys: Depth, richness, cinematic quality with 2D assets.
options.vs: Foreground/midground/background is a three-plane special case; layered depth may use many planes including exploded UI layers.
options.prompt: Separate the scene into 3-6 planes with perspective 1200px on the parent; far planes translateZ -400 to -800px, near planes +100px. On camera moves, pan the parent so planes parallax naturally; optionally explode UI layers apart along z over 900ms ease power3.inOut.

options.what: Three distinct depth planes, each with a role: framing foreground, subject midground, context background.
options.looks: Blurred or dark foreground elements at frame edges, sharp subject in the middle, simple background.
options.motion: Foreground moves fastest, background slowest; rack-focus between planes.
options.use: Cinematic brand films, illustrated scenes, product-in-environment shots.
options.vs: Layered depth is the general technique; three-plane composition is a classic cinematographic arrangement with defined roles.
options.prompt: Build three planes: foreground framing elements at frame edges (blur 6px, darker), midground subject sharp at center, background low-contrast. On camera moves, foreground moves 1.5x, midground 1x, background 0.3x the pan distance.

options.what: One physical or rendered object carries the frame, lit and presented like a product shot.
options.looks: Object centered or on a third, clean backdrop, studio lighting, reflections or contact shadow.
options.motion: Slow turntable rotation, camera orbit, macro push-ins on details.
options.use: Hardware launches, packaging, premium consumer products, logo objects.
options.vs: Centered hero can be type or UI; single-object hero is a physical object.
options.prompt: Present one object at 40-55% of frame height on a seamless backdrop, soft key light top-left, rim light right, contact shadow below. Rotate it slowly (rotationY 20 degrees over 4s, ease sine.inOut) with a 3-5% camera push-in.

options.what: Many elements move together in coordinated patterns, forming and reforming arrangements.
options.looks: Dozens of shapes, cards or icons arranged in formations that change.
options.motion: Staggered group moves, formations morphing, flocking, synchronized hits.
options.use: Brand stings, abstract explainers, feature abundance, music-driven pieces.
options.vs: Temporal composition is about layout states over time; choreography is about many elements moving in concert within or between them.
options.prompt: Animate 20-60 elements as one choreography: move them between 3-4 formations (grid, circle, line, logo shape) using stagger from 'center' or 'edges' (each 15-25ms), 700ms ease power3.inOut per move, with formations landing on beats.

options.what: Type is the primary visual; other elements support it.
options.looks: Large type dominates the frame, minimal imagery, layout decisions driven by words.
options.motion: Kinetic typography, text reflows, words as transitions.
options.use: Manifestos, brand films, social ads, launch teasers without product shots.
options.vs: UI-led puts the interface first; illustration-led puts drawn imagery first.
options.prompt: Let type carry the frame: headline at 120-300px occupying 40-80% of the frame, imagery limited to small supporting crops or none. Every scene is built around one line of copy; transitions happen through the type itself.

options.what: The product interface is the primary visual; type and graphics annotate it.
options.looks: Large UI views or crops filling most of the frame, callouts and labels around them.
options.motion: UI interactions, zooms into details, cursor-led demos, panels expanding.
options.use: SaaS launches, feature demos, product tours.
options.vs: Typography-led puts words first; illustration-led uses drawn imagery. Browser window and phone composition are containers for UI-led work.
options.prompt: Make the interface the hero: UI occupies 60-85% of the frame, zoomed crops for detail beats, type limited to short callouts (under 6 words) placed beside the UI, never over key controls.

options.what: Drawn imagery (characters, scenes, metaphors) is the primary visual.
options.looks: Full illustrated scenes, spot illustrations, metaphors carrying meaning; UI and type secondary.
options.motion: Character animation, scene transitions, metaphors transforming.
options.use: Explainers, onboarding, brand stories, abstract concepts that UI cannot show.
options.vs: UI-led shows the actual product; illustration-led shows ideas and metaphors.
options.prompt: Carry each scene with an illustration (character, scene or visual metaphor) occupying 50-80% of the frame; type is a short caption; UI appears only as simplified drawn elements in the same illustration style.

options.what: The composition is designed as a sequence of layouts over time, with the transitions between layouts treated as design decisions.
options.looks: No single frame summarizes it: e.g. one centered element, which splits into a multi-card grid, then one card expands into full-screen UI.
options.motion: Layout-to-layout transitions (Flip), a persistent anchor element carried through every state, elements born from and collapsing into each other.
options.use: Launch films, feature summaries, any piece longer than a few seconds.
options.conveys: Continuity, intelligence, a story told through structure.
options.vs: Transitions dimension covers how scenes cut or wipe; temporal composition covers how one continuous frame reorganizes itself. Multi-object choreography is movement; temporal composition is the sequence of layouts.
options.prompt: Plan the composition as 3-4 layout states (e.g. centered single element, then 2x3 card grid, then full-screen UI). Keep one anchor element continuous across every change; animate each change with GSAP Flip over 700-900ms ease power3.inOut; alternate sparse and dense states.
